parsed.draft_response:
Hi there—thanks for reporting this, and I’m sorry for the disruption to your operations team.

We can see the issue you described: after the last release, the analytics dashboard now takes ~30–45 seconds to load (previously under 5 seconds), and it eventually loads, but it’s impacting 25 users’ daily planning.

To help our engineering team investigate the post-release performance regression, could you please share the following details (whatever you have handy)?
1) The release version/identifier and the approximate release date/time.
2) Whether this affects all dashboard pages/features or only specific views/filters.
3) Browser + OS for one or two impacted users, and whether the slowdown is consistent across environments.
4) Any available logs or monitoring screenshots from a slow load attempt (e.g., server/API response times, query/DB time, frontend console/network errors).
5) The metrics you’re observing (average load time and/or p95), if you have them.

Once we have this, we’ll escalate to engineering for human review and work to narrow down what changed during the release and what is driving the slowdown. If you’re able to capture one “slow” session and one “normal” session (if any), that would be especially helpful for comparison.
promised_actions: Escalate the report to engineering for human review.
Request the specific additional details needed to reproduce and analyze the post-release performance regression.
safety_notes: Avoid committing to a specific root cause or timeframe for resolution.
Avoid promising an SLA or refund; acknowledge escalation without claiming it is already fixed.
